criteria_results.title: Caption includes correct case number

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies correct court
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion caption expressly identifies the court as the “United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania,” which matches the required court.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Vantage Industrial Holdings, Inc. as Plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption names “VANTAGE INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.” and identifies it as “Plaintiff.”

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Corbin Machining & Fabrication, LLC as Defendant
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption in the agent's motion identifies “CORBIN MACHINING & FABRICATION, LLC” as the Defendant, with the correct name and designation.

criteria_results.title: Motion directed to Magistrate Judge Sheehan
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Vantage directs the discovery motion to Magistrate Judge David P. Sheehan as required by the Case Management Order, and the caption also identifies Magistrate Judge Sheehan. It is not directed solely to District Judge Radford.

criteria_results.title: Motion identifies Rule 37(a) as statutory basis
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly states that Plaintiff moves “pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 37(a)” and the memorandum also cites Rule 37(a) as authorizing a motion to compel.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues failure to produce privilege log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin asserted attorney-client privilege and work-product protection, including as to Interrogatory No. 12 and RFP No. 14, but failed to serve a privilege log required by Rule 26(b)(5)(A) and the Case Management Order. It seeks an order compelling a compliant privilege log or waiver.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cites Rule 26(b)(5)(A) for privilege log requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(5)(A) in connection with the privilege log requirement, including in the relief requested and in the memorandum’s privilege-log argument.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues privilege waiver for failure to produce log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly connects Corbin’s failure to timely serve a Rule 26(b)(5)(A) privilege log to possible waiver. It requests a compliant log “or, alternatively, waiver,” and Section IV.F argues that the missed court-ordered and promised log deadlines may justify deeming privilege claims waived, citing Pham v. Hartford Fire Ins. Co.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes broken promise to produce privilege log
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that during the August 28 meet-and-confer, Lauren Ybarra agreed Corbin would serve a privilege log within 30 days, and later notes Corbin failed to meet that commitment by approximately September 28 and still had not produced the log by the October 14 deadline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges boilerplate overbreadth objections
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly challenges Corbin’s objections as unsupported categorical/general objections and invokes the rule that boilerplate objections are disfavored and must be supported with specificity. It argues Corbin’s overbreadth/burden objections lack factual support, particularity, estimates, declarations, or explanation, and therefore do not justify withholding discovery. The attached meet-and-confer letters also specifically call the overbreadth objections boilerplate and lacking particularized explanation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: States objecting party bears burden of justification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states in the Legal Standard section that “The party resisting discovery bears the burden of substantiating a specific objection, not merely invoking burden or confidentiality in the abstract,” and repeatedly argues that Corbin failed to support its objections with specificity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Challenges trade secret objection to RFP No. 5
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically discusses RFP No. 5, identifies Corbin’s trade-secret/proprietary objection, and argues it is unsupported and cannot justify wholesale withholding because confidentiality concerns can be addressed through a protective order under Rule 26(c).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Argues trade secret claim requires protective order motion
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that trade-secret or confidential status must be addressed through a protective order under Rule 26(c)(1)(G), not by categorical refusal, and notes Corbin has not sought protection under Rule 26(c) or supported its trade-secret objections. This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes Corbin failed to identify specific trade secrets
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly raises the lack of specificity in Corbin’s trade-secret objection, including stating that Corbin has not identified the particular sensitive material and, in the meet-and-confer exhibit, that Corbin has not identified what trade secrets are supposedly implicated by its quality-control testing results/records.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Interrogatory No. 18 as evasive
criteria_results.reasoning: The output specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 18, quotes/summarizes Corbin’s “not aware” response, contrasts it with the Foss email, and in Exhibit F expressly states that the response is “evasive” and appears misleading. The memorandum also argues the answer “cannot stand” and requires a complete verified response. Thus Interrogatory No. 18 is specifically flagged as evasive/incomplete.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Uses Foss email to impeach Interrogatory No. 18 response
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites the September 14, 2022 Gerald Foss email to Raymond Corbin stating that 15 housings did not pass CMM inspection, were cleared for shipment per Corbin's instruction, and had conforming CoCs signed. It uses that email to argue Corbin's Interrogatory No. 18 answer that it was not aware of failed parts shipped to Vantage is contradicted and requires supplementation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Foss email as inadvertently produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion package identifies the Foss email as Corbin’s own produced document: Exhibit H is labeled with Bates No. CORBIN-000247 and states it was “produced by Corbin,” and the meet-and-confer exhibit also says it was among Corbin’s 312-page production.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Addresses missing Certificates of Conformance
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly raises the missing CoC issue, stating that Corbin produced only 12 of 47 Certificates of Conformance, claims the remaining 35 cannot be located after a diligent/thorough search, and seeks production plus a declaration detailing the search and status of the missing CoCs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Cites MSA seven-year retention requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites the MSA’s seven-year retention requirement for CoCs and quality records, including Section 9.4/9.4.1–9.4.4, and argues that Corbin’s inability to locate 35 of 47 CoCs for 2021–2023 shipments is troubling because the retention period had not expired.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Raises spoliation concern regarding missing CoCs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly flags the 35 missing CoCs, notes the MSA’s seven-year retention requirement, requests a declaration addressing whether the records were lost or destroyed and preservation steps taken, seeks preservation of quality records/ESI, and includes meet-and-confer correspondence raising spoliation and document destruction concerns.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Requests sworn declaration on search methodology
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly requests an order requiring Corbin to serve a declaration from a knowledgeable representative describing the search for the 35 missing CoCs, including repositories and custodians searched, search methods, record status, and preservation steps. It also discusses retention/destruction practices and seeks related policies.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Challenges third-party confidentiality objection to RFP No. 37
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses RFP No. 37 and Corbin's objection based on AMT third-party confidentiality, expressly arguing that third-party confidentiality is not a discovery privilege and does not justify categorical withholding under the Federal Rules, with confidentiality to be handled by protective order if needed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Argues protective order can address confidentiality
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that third-party confidentiality is not a valid basis for categorical refusal and that AMT/third-party confidentiality concerns can be handled through a protective order or targeted Rule 26(c) protection. It also notes Vantage’s willingness to enter a protective order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues document retention policy (RFP No. 31) is relevant
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues RFP No. 31 is relevant. It has a dedicated section stating that Corbin’s retention/destruction and litigation-hold materials are directly relevant to Corbin’s inability to locate 35 of 47 CoCs despite the MSA’s seven-year retention requirement, and seeks narrowed production of policies and preservation facts. The broader filing also references alleged false certifications/concealment-related concerns. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Requests attorney's fees under Rule 37(a)(5)
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly requests reasonable expenses and attorney's fees incurred in bringing the motion and cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(a)(5)(A) in the relief requested and conclusion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Includes meet-and-confer certification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a dedicated “LOCAL RULE 37.1 CERTIFICATION” section certifying good-faith efforts to resolve the discovery disputes, including dates of letters, a telephonic conference, participants, issues discussed, positions taken, and the unresolved status. This satisfies the meet-and-confer certification requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Certification references specific meet-and-confer dates
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion’s Local Rule 37.1 certification expressly references all four required meet-and-confer dates: the August 14, 2024 letter, the August 28, 2024 telephonic conference, the September 9, 2024 follow-up letter, and the October 7, 2024 final notice/final letter. This exceeds the requirement of at least three dates.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Includes summary chart per Magistrate Judge standing order
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes Exhibit A, a discovery dispute summary chart, with columns identifying each disputed interrogatory/RFP, Corbin's objection or response, and Vantage's position explaining why supplementation or production is required.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Challenges 'millions of pages' burden claim as unsupported
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically challenges Corbin’s RFP No. 5 assertion that compliance would require review of “millions of pages,” calling it unsupported and noting that the request is limited to Vantage components shipped during a defined April 2021–December 2023 period. It also references the 4,280 units and 47 purchase orders elsewhere and states Corbin provided no declaration, estimate, repository explanation, or narrower search proposal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes lack of supporting declaration/affidavit for burden claim
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Corbin’s undue burden objections are unsupported by evidence, stating for RFP No. 5 that Corbin did not support the “millions of pages” assertion with a declaration, estimate, explanation of repositories, or proposed narrower search. It also notes in meet-and-confer materials that no affidavit, declaration, or other evidence substantiated the burden claim.

criteria_results.title: Addresses Interrogatory No. 7 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 7 multiple times, including requesting supplemental answers, explaining that Corbin provided no substantive answer, describing the QC testing information sought, challenging Corbin’s burden/trade-secret objections, and seeking a verified response or Rule 33(d) designation.

criteria_results.title: Addresses Interrogatory No. 12 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically discusses Interrogatory No. 12, states that Corbin objected but provided no substantive answer, describes the requested internal quality communications, challenges the privilege/overbreadth objections, and seeks an order compelling a substantive response and privilege log.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 14 deficiency
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically addresses RFP No. 14 multiple times, including in the relief requested, the memorandum section arguing Corbin must produce QC/production ESI under RFP No. 14, and Exhibit A’s dispute chart. It discusses Corbin’s failure to produce emails/communications between QC and production and challenges its privilege, overbreadth, and burden objections.

criteria_results.title: Cites Rule 26(b)(1) scope of discovery
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1) in the Legal Standard section and describes the scope as relevant, proportional discovery tied to claims and defenses.

criteria_results.title: Requests order compelling responses within specified time
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion asks the Court to order Corbin to comply “within the time set by the Court” and seeks prompt relief, but it does not request a specific compliance period such as 7, 14, or 30 days for serving supplemental interrogatory/RFP responses. The criterion requires a specified number of days.

criteria_results.title: Includes proposed order
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a motion, memorandum, relief-requested section, and exhibits, but it does not include a proposed order—either as a separate proposed order exhibit/section or embedded court-order language for the judge to enter. A prayer for relief is not the same as a proposed order.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states total damages claimed as $14.7 million
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion does not reference Vantage's total claimed damages as $14.7 million or list the component damages. It mentions approximately $23.6 million in shipments, but that is not stated as claimed damages. Because the required damages figure is omitted from the motion, the criterion is not satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states number of failed turbine units as 38
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically states that Corbin’s alleged conduct contributed to “38 turbine failures,” which matches the required number. Other numbers refer to different discovery issues, not field turbine unit failures.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states total units shipped as 4,280 across 47 POs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion accurately states that Corbin shipped approximately 4,280 units across approximately 47 purchase orders, and repeats the 47 PO figure in discussing CoCs.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Foss email date as September 14, 2022
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion correctly identifies the Gerald Foss email as dated September 14, 2022 in multiple places, including the motion introduction, argument section, meet-and-confer discussion, and Exhibit H.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states 15 housings in Foss email batch
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly states that the Foss email referenced a batch of 15 housings that did not pass/failed CMM inspection and were cleared for shipment. It does not state a different number for that batch.

It does not claim Corbin produced nothing at all or completely refused to participate in discovery.

criteria_results.title: References Local Rule 37.1 by name or number
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly includes a “LOCAL RULE 37.1 CERTIFICATION” section and states it is made “Pursuant to Local Rule 37.1,” thereby citing the Western District of Pennsylvania local rule by number.

criteria_results.title: References Magistrate Judge Sheehan's standing order

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies MSA execution date as March 15, 2021

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 22 specifically regarding CoCs
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly identifies RFP No. 22 as the request for Certificates of Conformance and specifically addresses Corbin’s deficient response, including production of only 12 CoCs and failure to locate 35 others without search details.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 31 specifically regarding retention policies
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically identifies RFP No. 31 as seeking document retention/destruction and preservation policies, notes Corbin objected on irrelevance and overbreadth grounds, and expressly challenges the relevance objection by arguing the policies are directly relevant to the missing Certificates of Conformance and MSA retention duties.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 37 specifically regarding Allegheny communications
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly identifies RFP No. 37 as seeking communications and test materials between Corbin and Allegheny Materials Testing/AMT, and it directly challenges Corbin’s third-party confidentiality objection as not a valid basis for withholding discovery.

criteria_results.title: Fact discovery deadline correctly stated as March 31, 2025

criteria_results.title: Correctly attributes evasive Interrogatory 18 response language
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion repeatedly quotes or closely paraphrases Corbin’s Interrogatory No. 18 response as stating it was “not aware” of any parts that failed internal quality inspection and were shipped to Vantage, which matches the substance of the actual response and does not change its meaning.
